name: Secrets
summary: A Cold War hidden-team bluffing game where CIA, KGB and Hippies trade Character cards and swap identities.
rules_text: Each player gets a secret Identity token: CIA, KGB, or Hippie, plus one hidden center token. On your turn draw Character cards until you have two different types, then secretly keep one to offer facedown to another player. You may lie about it. The target must accept it into their face-up display or refuse so it goes to you. Each Character triggers an effect when placed: Detective lets you secretly peek at any Identity, Psychiatrist swaps two others' Identities, Double Agent swaps yours with the center, Politician goes to another's display and lets you peek theirs, Journalist forces you to reveal your own Identity without seeing it, Diplomat reveals center then secretly swaps it left or right, Scientist wipes your own display to zero after two, Assassin gives a facedown Bullet (-0 to -3) to someone. Identical pair in a display flips to zero. The player with the fewest total cards holds the UN token and may steal an Offer. Game ends when a display reaches 5 cards (4 cards with 7-8 players). If one Hippie alone has the lowest personal total, they win alone; otherwise CIA and KGB sum their members' face-up values and higher team wins.
rating_reason: Secret identity team game, hidden roles, bluffing, fits hidden_hands roles_with_allies
